incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: continuous-batching.p99 > 1200ms (streaming path) in us-west-2 - triggered by SLO watcher at 2025-11-12T03:12:00Z
Ben S: I'm on it. seeing p95 ~ 300ms, p99 ~ 1.25s for streaming endpoints routed to cont-batcher.
Alice M: Confirmed from dashboards — tail spikes correlate with mixed sequence length workload from embeddings pipeline.
Dan R: Any 5xxs? customer-impact?
Ben S: A few client-visible stalls, some streaming sessions timed out (408). No mass 5xxs. Customer Ops says two larger customers reported degraded interactive latency.
Customer Ops: Customer A (ecom-search) reports slow chat responses for ~15m. Customer B (docs-index) had occasional session disconnects. Both on Hosted tier in us-west-2.
Erin L: Posting recent trace snippet, looks like scheduling delay before batch execution:
```
scheduler.enqueue_time=2025-11-12T03:11:47.123Z
batch_formed_time=2025-11-12T03:12:01.874Z  # ~14.7s wait
kv_lookup=2ms
kernel_exec=120ms
```
Ben S: That enqueue->batch gap is the culprit. Continuous batching is pulling together long-waiting small seq requests behind long sequences. mixed seq length causing batch holdouts.
Alice M: Also seeing KV cache thrash on those long sequences — cache misses spike, causing extra work and slowing scheduling.
Cara P: Recommended live mitigations?
Ben S: Priorities: 1) Stop batching streaming endpoints to restore low-latency path. 2) Adjust scheduler fairness to avoid long queries blocking small ones. 3) If necessary, reduce max_batch_size and enable kv-ttl-adaptive.
Erin L: Quick config we can flip in Console:
```
route: /v1/stream
service.runtime.continuous_batching.enabled = false
service.runtime.scheduler.share_alpha = 0.35  # more fair to short jobs
service.runtime.batching.max_batch_size = 32  # down from 128
kv.cache.adaptive_ttl = true
```
Ben S: I'll run hotfix 1 (disable cont batch for streaming) now. Will also add a temporary canary rule so only us-west-2 streaming routes get change first.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: starting rollout: hotfix/disable-contbatch-streaming -> us-west-2 (canary=10%) by Ben S at 2025-11-12T03:16:02Z
Ben S: Ran the rollout command: `rctl rollout apply hotfix/disable-contbatch-streaming --region=us-west-2 --canary=10`
Alice M: Watching metrics... p99 dropped from 1.25s -> 420ms within canary slice. p95 down to ~180ms.
Ben S: Expanding canary to 50%.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout at 50% -> success.
Cara P: I'll take over ops for the rest of the window — Ben, can you doc the changes and handoff any follow-ups?
Ben S: Handing off TO Cara P. Notes: disabled cont batch on streaming routes, reduced max_batch_size to 32 cluster-wide as temporary, set share_alpha=0.35. Also scheduled a KV cache rebuild for affected nodes (job queued).
Cara P: Acknowledged. Next steps: monitor SLOs for 30m, then either re-enable cont-batching with smarter seq-length partitioning or keep streaming off continuous path and route to low-latency executor.
Customer Ops: Both customers report improvement after ~7 minutes of canary expansion. No new complaints.
Erin L: For root cause ticket — hypothesis: continuous-batching scheduler favors throughput and inadvertently groups long sequences with short streams when sequence length predictor underestimates variance. That + KV thrash = head-of-line blocking.
Ben S: Proposed long-term mitigations: - seq-length-aware bucketing (pre-batch partition on seq length) - dynamic max-wait per priority class - scheduler preemption for streaming (preempt large batches if short jobs queue up) - KV cache smarter eviction (pin small/stream prefixes)
Alice M: Also run an eval on the embedding pipeline to see if it can be throttled or rate-limited during peak to reduce variance.
Cara P: I'll open incident ticket INC-2025-2314 and link this thread. Will include customer-impact notes and mitigation steps.
Cara P: Assigning follow-ups: @Ben S to implement seq-length bucketing prototype (P0 for infra-ml collab). @Erin L to run KV cache simulation + metrics. @Dan R to prepare rollback-playbook for toggles in case reintroduction causes regression.
Ben S: Quick note on rollback commands if needed: `rctl rollout rollback hotfix/disable-contbatch-streaming --to=0% --region=us-west-2`

Ben S: TL;DR: Live mitigation applied (disabled continuous batching for streaming, made scheduler more fair, lowered max batch). Impact: restored tail latency, minor throughput hit expected, follow-ups created for seq-aware batching and KV improvements.
